:::{#def-laplace}
#### Laplace distribution

A random variable $Y$ has the **Laplace distribution**
with location parameter $\mean \in \reals$ and scale parameter $b > 0$,
written $Y \sim \dLaplacef{\mean, b}$,
if $Y$ is continuous with [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf):

$$\p(Y=y) \eqdef \frac{1}{2b} \ef{-\frac{\abs{y - \mean}}{b}}, \quad y \in \reals$$ {#eq-laplace-pdf}

:::

::: {.remark .notes}
The [normal density](random-variables.qmd#def-normal) has the squared distance $(y - \mean)^2$ in its exponent.
The Laplace density has the absolute distance $\abs{y - \mean}$ instead.
Both densities are symmetric about $\mean$,
but the Laplace density has a sharp peak at $\mean$ and decays more slowly in the tails.
:::
